summary: Posterior probability set at 0.17 (17%) for any state-actor chemical weapons use in Ukraine before May 1, 2026, derived from a Bayesian update on the reference class anchored near 12%.
Upward updates come from OPCW-confirmed presence of CS and related agents on frontlines and credible intelligence reporting increased use (chloropicrin/CS) by Russia.
Downward pressure from deterrence measures (EU sanctions, enhanced monitoring) and analyses suggesting limited or targeted incidents rather than mass-scale deployment temper the risk.
Attribution ambiguity and ongoing investigations keep certainty moderate; risk remains nonzero but not highly certain.

justification.synthesis_rationale: The 17% posterior emerges from anchoring to a modest baseline in the reference class and applying multiple, partially correlated updates. Strong upward signals from OPCW detections and credible intelligence are tempered by sanctions, normative constraints, and attribution uncertainty, which together prevent the posterior from rising toward the raw, high-end estimates. Calibration accounts for potential factor correlation and the limited horizon, yielding a modest, nonzero risk estimate with a 12–22% plausible range.
